This Corporate Procedure (CP) describes the general cross-functional approach that Boehringer Ingelheim (BI) has developed and adopted for the process of Computerized Systems Validation (CSV).

This CP is mandatory for all BI Units that use Computerized Systems or develop, release or distribute software applications or application software considered to be a medical device that are regulated by current GxP. In case of other regulatory requirements in the context of medicinal products for human or veterinary use require validation, this Corporate Procedure must be followed. Within BI Computerized Systems includes “Equipment”, “Computer System”, and “Spreadsheet”.
See Reference Document to this CP, Roles and Definitions (see RD00).

LeVA (Lean Validation Approach) is the BI’s global standard approach for validation of computerized systems.

elements.text: Reading this document in the current learning management system (LMS) will be the implementation of this CP update.
This CP is intended to give an overview of the global principles and structure of BI´s Computerized System validation program.

This CP as well as the subordinated Corporate SOPs and templates are legally binding on local level, giving due respect to local law and regulations if necessary. Templates are mandatory within every function in the scope of these documents and no additional local regulations are required (except where required by local law). The local unit must only to ensure that these documents become binding on the local level.
Each Boehringer Ingelheim Entity is responsible for compliance with this CP, the Corporate SOPs and their associated mandatory templates.
Global/Divisional/Local MSO for CSV must follow the BI Quality Manual (see RD00 for reference) responsibilities for the management of the Computerized System Validation Quality System.

The reference document Roles and Definitions to this CP defines the additional roles and responsibilities required for the Computerized Systems Validation processes. This includes also the roles and responsibility associated with specific tasks, assignments and deliverables which are described within the Corporate SOPs based on the class of the system.
The following table summarizes the additional, main responsibilities regarding the CSV document hierarchy:

cells.text: The global MSO specifies, maintains and optimizes the Computerized System Validation framework at global level, giving strategic and conceptual guidance to the organization with respect to the Computerized System validation process.

The global GPO for each of the different system classes (Equipment, Computer System and Spreadsheets) develop, continuous improve and implement the cross-function Corporate SOPs and associated mandatory templates.

The local/functional Quality Unit ensures the local/functional implementation 1 and release of this CP, Corporate SOPs and their associated templates, or where identified, at the divisional level. Explain this CP and Corporate SOPs in case of a (local) Audit/Inspection.

A cross-functional and cross-divisional board, chaired by Head of Corporate Division Quality, that is responsible for steering the CSV System by endorsing compliance governance and management policies.

elements.text: While the structure of the process described in this document and further delineated in subject specific Corporate SOPs is designed to follow industry good practice and regulations (i.e. GAMP, ICH, FDA, EMA), Boehringer Ingelheim does not promote nor support a “one size fits all” approach to validation of Computerized Systems. Wherever appropriate, activities must be evaluated carefully for a “right sized” effort using the Boehringer Ingelheim Risk Based Approach to Computerized Systems Validation.

Certain application systems can contain a mix of GxP and Non-GxP functionality and/or processes. Under these conditions, application of the full validation life cycle to the entire system may impose disproportionate effort. Using a risk based approach. it may be possible to reduce the effort of validating such systems while remaining compliant with the overall Boehringer Ingelheim approach to computer system validation. Please see reference document Risk Based Approach to non-GxP Functions within GxP Relevant Computer Systems for further guidance on this topic.

1 The Corp. Procedure as well as the subordinated Corp. SOPs/templates are legally binding on local level, giving due respect to local law and regulations if necessary. Templates are mandatory within every function in the scope of these documents and no additional local regulations are required (except where required by local law), the local unit has only to ensure that these documents become binding on the local level.

Boehringer Ingelheim expects that where a computerized system handles data, data integrity must be ensured, irrespective of the format in which the data is generated, is recorded, processed, retained and used to ensure a complete, consistent and accurate record throughout the data life cycle. The LeVA framework includes an assessment of the Data Integrity compliance for computerized systems following the principles described in the CP on Data Integrity Governance within Boehringer Ingelheim (see RD00 for reference).
Boehringer Ingelheim has one core process that is valid globally for the validation of Computerized Systems based on Corporate SOPs .

No local departures or adaptations are permitted except where local laws require it. The Global Management System Owner (GMSO) and Global Process Owner(s) (GPO) may permit exceptions for translations to a local language on a case-by-case basis

Software applications that are developed, released and distributed that are considered medical devices must meet the requirements of local regulatory requirements that govern such technology, such as 21 CFR Part 820 in the United States.
Prospective validation is the process of validating a Computerized System prior to using it in a production environment. For new Computerized Systems the prospective validation approach must be used.

For Computerized Systems it must be considered available and novel technologies that guarantee intended use including regulatory compliance requirements in scope. Where a computerized system replaces a manual operation, there should be no resulting decrease in product quality, process control or quality assurance and no increase in the overall risk of the process.

Boehringer Ingelheim expects that application software purchased for GxP activities that employ the use of electronic records and signatures will comply  with relevant regulatory requirements (e.g. 21 CFR Part 11, Annex 11) as delivered.

Boehringer Ingelheim strongly promotes the use of paperless environments and electronic workflows for SLC documents. In order to increase data integrity compliance, paper processes should be replaced by qualified electronic workflows wherever possible and reasonable.
Once the Computerized System is deemed validated and released to production use, appropriate actions must be taken to ensure the system remains in a validated state.

All relevant Computerized Systems must be maintained in an inventory; GxP relevant Computerized Systems as well as Computerized Systems evaluated as non-GxP relevant as determined by a documented validation determination. The inventory will typically be owned by the responsible QA organisation or CSV&C function and must contain at minimum: 
Name of computerized system
Name of software applications, if applicable
Unique identifier for the computer system / equipment / Excel-Spreadsheet
Short description of the functionality
Current major version number(s) of main component(s) or a reference to a version log, if applicable
Name of System Owner
System class (i.e computer system / equipment / spreadsheet)
System status (i.e. in planning / operation / retired)
As of date for current system status
GxP relevance (i.e. yes / no)
Next Periodic Review date

For the system classes of Computer Systems and Spreadsheets (global and local), the IT Service Management System tool is mandatory to maintain a global system list, containing the above mentioned elements.

Boehringer Ingelheim expects that users will be appropriately trained; the procedures required for the system’s maintenance and operation are in place and remain current and that formal change control is practiced. Changes of Computerized Systems must follow the Corporate Procedure Change Management (see RD00 for reference).
Boehringer Ingelheim also expects a periodic review for each system in order to evaluate the possible impact of changes on the system over time.

6.1.1 Risk Based Approach for Computerized System Validation

Boehringer Ingelheim supports the use of a “Risk Based Approach” for the validation of Computerized Systems. The intention of the risk based approach is to evaluate the risk(s) associated with a computerized system as they relate to human safety, product efficacy and quality and to conclude if the risks (or absence thereof) allow for an abbreviated and compact validation approach.

The risk based approach evaluation is part of the Validation Plan and forms the basis and justification for the specific validation approach. The specific validation approach should consider (but is not limited to) the:

items: Software category (Configured / Non-Configured Product or Custom Application, etc.)
Intended use of the Computerized System i.e. what impact does the Computerized System have on safety, product efficacy and/or product/data quality
Experience with the system and/or supplier (confidence in system quality)

elements.text: The results of the evaluation of the factors above will determine the amount and detail of validation or qualification documentation and testing to be produced.
6.1.2 System Specific Risk Assessment

During the validation project, a prospective risk assessment on requirement / function / interface level must be done to analyze all issues that could affect the operation and reliability of the Computerized System. The level of detail of the Risk Assessment should correlate to the overall system risk, e.g. for low risk systems, a statement within the validation plan could be sufficient.

For the purpose of evaluating application systems for potential risks, BI follows among other things the GAMP categorization for system types (i.e. Configured / Non-Configured Product or Custom Application).
6.1.3 Supplier Assessment

Boehringer Ingelheim expects that the suppliers of software and hardware should be evaluated carefully to ensure that products procured for the Company are of high quality and will meet the requirements for use in a GxP environment. The decisions to perform supplier audits must be documented, based both on regulatory and business risk.

The requirements described in the reference document Internal Requirements for Use for Cloud Computing of GxP Applications (see RD00 for reference) must be considered for supplier assessments of cloud solutions for GxP activities.
Wherever possible and appropriate, duplicate work should be avoided. As an example, there should be no retesting of functionality when suitable vendor testing documentation is available.
6.1.4 Traceability

A key task within the project and system life cycle is to ensure appropriate traceability. Traceability links the user requirements, risk analysis, functional specifications, design specifications, and all formal testing in a methodical and easy-to-follow manner. The traceability between these documents is crucial to the quality of the system. It ensures that all specifications can be traced to a test or verification activity, where applicable. A risk assessment must state explicitly if the selected system has certain specifications that are unmet or will not be implemented.
6.1.5 Cloud Computing

Boehringer Ingelheim recognizes that cloud computing processes such as SaaS (software as a service) IaaS (infrastructure as a service) and PaaS (platform as a service) can provide financial benefits and add to efficiency. Careful examination of cloud environments to ensure safe guarding of the Company’s assets must be assured in any instance where we employ the use of a cloud solution. When the Company engages in the use of cloud solutions for GxP activities additional considerations must be taken into account. Employing a cloud solution for a GxP process does not alter our statutory responsibility to ensure all of our obligations to meet regulatory requirements and expectations are consistently met. Boehringer Ingelheim cannot delegate these responsibilities to an external party.

Boehringer Ingelheim has established requirements for use of cloud solutions for GxP activities both on the part of the provider as well as BI’s internal obligations, in the reference document Internal Requirements for Use for Cloud Computing of GxP Applications and the Corporate SOP on Cloud Computing and External Hosting of BI Data (see RD00 for both references). The purpose of these procedures is to ensure that system validation and qualification activities will occur as if BI were internally implementing, controlling and maintaining such systems. It is not the intent of this reference document to establish criteria for cloud providers to adopt the Boehringer Ingelheim LeVA approach, but only to show substantial similarity to it.
6.1.6 Mobile Technologies

Boehringer Ingelheim recognizes that mobile technologies, including but not limited to mobile apps, devices, sensors etc., are being used in GxP processes to support regulated activities. The use of these mobile technologies impose additional risks which must be addressed during implementation and validation of these mobile technologies. To ensure that system validation and qualification activities will occur to identify and mitigate the risks associated with the use of mobile technologies and to provide guidance on the application of the LeVA framework to support mobile technologies, the reference document on Considerations for application of LeVA for Mobile Technologies (see RD00) must be followed.

6.2.1 Corporate Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
The Boehringer Ingelheim Corporate SOPs for Computerized Systems validation are intended to be the sole reference to requirements for CSV globally.

All GxP-relevant Computerized Systems must be validated according to the Corporate SOP(s) referenced below (also see RD00 for specific references). If a system cannot clearly be classified into one of the class-specific Corporate SOPs, the final decision will be done by the System Owner, together with the respective QA, on which Corporate SOPs and associated templates will be used.
6.2.1.1 Corporate SOP – Validation of Equipment
This class of system represents the majority of systems found within Boehringer Ingelheim and includes Equipment with and without Computer Systems.

Equipment may consist of simple standardized components, interdependent equipment, systems that include automation, instrumentation, integrated process control and supervisory computerized controls (e.g. laboratory instrumentation, embedded controls, Programmable Logic Controller (PLC), utilities, facilities).
The System Life Cycle for Equipment is described in Corp. SOP on Validation of Equipment (see RD00).
6.2.1.2 Corporate SOP(s) – Validation of Computer Systems

This class of system generally will have an output that creates, analyzes, stores or transmits data and/or records. In some cases, they may have associated peripheral devices that are not considered in the same class as equipment. Equipment associated with this system class is typically referred to as “attached devices”. The Boehringer Ingelheim approach to validation of this class of system is generic because of the large number of different Computerized Systems. Standard templates, such as a Validation Plan, are used for system life cycle deliverables that are common across all systems.
The requirements for Computer Systems are described in the following set of documents (also see RD00): 
Corporate SOP on Validation of Computer Systems
Corporate SOP on Computer System Design and Installation
Corporate SOP on Computer System Software Development
Corporate SOP on Operational Use of Computer Systems
6.2.1.3 Corporate SOP – Validation of Spreadsheets

Excel spreadsheets are used throughout the BI organization for a broad variety of GxP data processing activities – from analytical methods to stability release processes. The system life cycle for Spreadsheets (e.g. created with Microsoft Excel) is described in Corporate  SOP on Validation of Spreadsheets
6.2.2 SLC Documentation – Based on Mandatory SLC templates

Boehringer Ingelheim will provide the BI user community with standard mandatory templates (refer to the reference document List of Templates for CSV Documentation , see RD00) to be used in the validation of the different system classes. While the format of these templates can be modified (e.g. letter size), the content is binding. Electronic systems may be used as a replacement of mandatory templates, provided that the mandatory content of the template is kept by the electronic system, and that the system has been validated.
The templates could consist of four different kinds of text/sections (the different text / sections will be marked with different colors within the templates

items: Mandatory text / sections b) Recommended text / sections c) Text / sections to be chosen from (e.g. two alternatives descriptions available) d) Instructions to guide / support the authors (must be deleted before the „document“ is finalized) If supplier provided SLC documentation may be used instead of LeVA templates if it is found to be adequate, meeting the requirements of our internal SOPs and their associated templates.

elements.text: Existing documents, such as test plans and test cases, should be reused wherever possible to realize greater efficiency.
6.2.3 Translation of Corporate SOPs and their associated templates
The Corporate SOPs and their associated templates are intended to be the sole reference to requirements for CSV globally.

The single exception to this requirement is if an obligation exists to have the SOPs translated to local language. Even in this case, the translated version will be based on the language and not location, i.e. only one translation per language will be allowed.
6.2.4 Translation of SLC Documents for Global Computerized Systems

In the event it becomes necessary to translate SLC documentation for Global Computerized Systems (e.g. original record in English and translated to Spanish for inspection or audit purposes) it is the responsibility of the local QA function to ensure the correct translation and fitness for local use.
